def apply_manifest_v2(
    manifest: dict[str, Any],
    *,
    archive: Mapping[str, Any] | None = None,
) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Add the v2 semantic contract while retaining v1 compatibility fields."""

    compatibility = manifest.get("compatibility") or {}
    legacy_schema = str(
        compatibility.get("legacySchema")
        or manifest.get("schema")
        or LEGACY_MAPLIBRE_SCHEMA
    )
    existing_layers = manifest.get("layers") if isinstance(manifest.get("layers"), dict) else {}
    resources: dict[str, dict[str, Any]] = {}
    layers: dict[str, dict[str, Any]] = {}
    legends: dict[str, dict[str, Any]] = deepcopy(manifest.get("legends") or {})

    for tileset in manifest.get("tilesets", []):
        display_resource, numeric_resource = _add_tileset_resources(resources, tileset)
        if tileset.get("type") == "vector":
            for legacy_layer in tileset.get("layers", []):
                layer_id = str(legacy_layer.get("id") or "")
                if not layer_id:
                    raise ValueError("Every vector viewer layer requires an id.")
                if layer_id in layers:
                    raise ValueError(f"Duplicate viewer layer id: {layer_id}")
                layers[layer_id] = _vector_layer_record(
                    legacy_layer,
                    tileset,
                    display_resource,
                )
        elif tileset.get("type") == "raster":
            layer_id = str(tileset.get("id") or "")
            if not layer_id:
                raise ValueError("Every raster viewer layer requires an id.")
            if layer_id in layers:
                raise ValueError(f"Duplicate viewer layer id: {layer_id}")
            legend_id, legend = _raster_legend(tileset)
            legends[legend_id] = legend
            layers[layer_id] = _raster_layer_record(
                tileset,
                display_resource,
                numeric_resource,
                legend_id,
            )

    raster_query = manifest.get("rasterQuery") or {}
    for resource in resources.values():
        if resource.get("type") != "cog":
            continue
        if raster_query.get("sourceCrs"):
            resource.setdefault("crs", raster_query["sourceCrs"])
        if raster_query.get("sourceProj4"):
            resource.setdefault("proj4", raster_query["sourceProj4"])

    # Incremental terrain/result packaging rebuilds the semantic contract from
    # compatibility tilesets. Retain context already enriched by the archive
    # so a later layer import cannot erase HEC-RAS plan and geometry titles.
    for layer_id, layer in layers.items():
        previous = existing_layers.get(layer_id)
        if not isinstance(previous, dict):
            continue
        _copy_present(
            previous,
            layer,
            "plan",
            "planTitle",
            "geometry",
            "geometryTitle",
            "terrain",
        )

    _add_hybrid_basemap(resources, layers)
    _enrich_layer_context(layers, archive)
    associations = _build_associations(manifest, layers, archive)
    tree = _build_tree(manifest, layers, archive, associations)
    interaction = _build_interaction(manifest, layers)
    capabilities = _build_capabilities(layers, archive)

    provenance = deepcopy(manifest.get("provenance") or {})
    provenance.setdefault("generatedBy", manifest.get("generatedBy", "ras2cng maplibre"))
    provenance.setdefault("sourceProject", manifest.get("sourceProject"))
    provenance.setdefault("sourceCrs", manifest.get("sourceCrs"))
    if archive:
        provenance.setdefault("archiveSchemaVersion", archive.get("schema_version"))
    provenance.setdefault(
        "resultSemantics",
        {
            "rawHdf": "Values at HEC-RAS computation elements; no surface interpolation.",
            "storedMap": "Raster surface generated by RASMapper/RasProcess.",
        },
    )

    manifest["schema"] = MAPLIBRE_SCHEMA
    manifest["resources"] = resources
    manifest["layers"] = layers
    manifest["tree"] = tree
    manifest["associations"] = associations
    manifest["legends"] = legends
    manifest["interaction"] = interaction
    manifest["capabilities"] = capabilities
    manifest.setdefault("timeAxes", {})
    manifest["provenance"] = provenance
    manifest["compatibility"] = {
        "legacySchema": legacy_schema,
        "legacyFields": ["tilesets", "groups"],
        "legacyViewerSupported": True,
    }
    validate_manifest_v2(manifest)
    return manifest

def validate_manifest_v2(manifest: Mapping[str, Any]) -> None:
    """Raise ``ValueError`` when required v2 references are inconsistent."""

    if manifest.get("schema") != MAPLIBRE_SCHEMA:
        raise ValueError(f"Viewer manifest schema must be {MAPLIBRE_SCHEMA!r}.")
    resources = manifest.get("resources")
    layers = manifest.get("layers")
    tree = manifest.get("tree")
    if not isinstance(resources, Mapping):
        raise ValueError("Viewer manifest resources must be an object.")
    if not isinstance(layers, Mapping):
        raise ValueError("Viewer manifest layers must be an object.")
    if not isinstance(tree, list):
        raise ValueError("Viewer manifest tree must be an array.")

    expected_roots = [root_id for root_id, _ in ROOT_DEFINITIONS]
    observed_roots = [node.get("id") for node in tree]
    if observed_roots != expected_roots:
        raise ValueError(
            "Viewer manifest roots must be ordered as " + ", ".join(expected_roots)
        )

    for layer_id, layer in layers.items():
        resource_id = layer.get("resource")
        if resource_id not in resources:
            raise ValueError(f"Layer {layer_id!r} references missing resource {resource_id!r}.")
        query = layer.get("query") or {}
        numeric_resource = query.get("numericResource")
        if numeric_resource and numeric_resource not in resources:
            raise ValueError(
                f"Layer {layer_id!r} references missing numeric resource {numeric_resource!r}."
            )
        domain_policy = (layer.get("style") or {}).get("domainPolicy", "fixed")
        if domain_policy == "current-view":
            legend_id = (layer.get("style") or {}).get("legendRef")
            legend = (manifest.get("legends") or {}).get(legend_id, {})
            if legend.get("type") == "categorical":
                raise ValueError(
                    f"Categorical layer {layer_id!r} cannot use current-view styling."
                )
            numeric = resources.get(numeric_resource, {})
            if numeric.get("type") != "cog":
                raise ValueError(
                    f"Current-view layer {layer_id!r} requires an authoritative numeric COG."
                )
            if not numeric.get("serviceAsset") or not numeric.get("serviceRevision"):
                raise ValueError(
                    f"Current-view layer {layer_id!r} requires serviceAsset and serviceRevision metadata."
                )
            service = (manifest.get("services") or {}).get("numericRaster") or {}
            if not all(
                service.get(key)
                for key in ("baseUrl", "statisticsPath", "samplePath", "tilePath")
            ):
                raise ValueError(
                    f"Current-view layer {layer_id!r} requires the numericRaster service contract."
                )

    tree_layer_ids: set[str] = set()

    def visit(node: Mapping[str, Any]) -> None:
        layer_id = node.get("layerId")
        if layer_id:
            if layer_id not in layers:
                raise ValueError(f"Tree references missing layer {layer_id!r}.")
            if layer_id in tree_layer_ids:
                raise ValueError(f"Tree references layer {layer_id!r} more than once.")
            tree_layer_ids.add(str(layer_id))
        for child in node.get("children", []):
            visit(child)

    for root in tree:
        visit(root)

    if tree_layer_ids != set(layers):
        missing = sorted(set(layers) - tree_layer_ids)
        raise ValueError("Viewer layers missing from semantic tree: " + ", ".join(missing))

    interaction = manifest.get("interaction") or {}
    active_layer = interaction.get("activeLayerId")
    if active_layer and active_layer not in layers:
        raise ValueError(f"Active layer {active_layer!r} does not exist.")
    for layer_id in interaction.get("pinnedLayerIds", []):
        if layer_id not in layers:
            raise ValueError(f"Pinned layer {layer_id!r} does not exist.")

docs.title: ras2cng.publication
docs.text: Validate an Example Library viewer bundle before public catalog admission.

docs.title: validate_example_publication(viewer_manifest, archive_manifest=None, *, check_files=True, check_http_ranges=False)
docs.text:
Run the strict RAS Commander Example Library publication gate.

Source code in ras2cng/publication.py 
def validate_example_publication(
    viewer_manifest: Path | Mapping[str, Any],
    archive_manifest: Path | Mapping[str, Any] | None = None,
    *,
    check_files: bool = True,
    check_http_ranges: bool = False,
) -> PublicationReport:
    """Run the strict RAS Commander Example Library publication gate."""

    manifest, manifest_path = _load_document(viewer_manifest)
    archive, archive_path = (
        _load_document(archive_manifest)
        if archive_manifest is not None
        else (None, None)
    )
    base_dir = manifest_path.parent if manifest_path else None
    report = PublicationReport(str(manifest_path or "<mapping>"))

    try:
        validate_manifest_v2(manifest)
    except Exception as error:
        report.add("error", "manifest.v2", str(error))

    resources = manifest.get("resources") if isinstance(manifest.get("resources"), Mapping) else {}
    layers = manifest.get("layers") if isinstance(manifest.get("layers"), Mapping) else {}
    completed_plan_ids = {
        str(plan.get("plan_id"))
        for plan in (archive or {}).get("results", [])
        if isinstance(plan, Mapping) and plan.get("completed") is True and plan.get("plan_id")
    }
    source_crs = (manifest.get("provenance") or {}).get("sourceCrs") or manifest.get("sourceCrs")
    if not source_crs:
        report.add("error", "project.crs", "The viewer manifest has no validated project CRS.")

    _validate_no_local_paths(manifest, report)
    _validate_resources(
        resources,
        report,
        base_dir=base_dir,
        check_files=check_files,
        check_http_ranges=check_http_ranges,
    )
    _validate_extent_color_service(manifest, resources, layers, report)

    geometry_layers = {
        layer_id: layer for layer_id, layer in layers.items()
        if layer.get("sourceKind") == "geometry"
    }
    extent_layers = {
        layer_id: layer for layer_id, layer in geometry_layers.items()
        if layer.get("role") == _MODEL_EXTENT_ROLE
    }
    geometry_ids = sorted(
        {
            str(layer.get("geometry"))
            for layer in geometry_layers.values()
            if layer.get("geometry")
        }
    )
    visible_geometry_ids = {
        str(layer.get("geometry"))
        for layer in geometry_layers.values()
        if layer.get("geometry") and layer.get("visible") is True
    }
    if geometry_ids and len(visible_geometry_ids) != 1:
        report.add(
            "error",
            "defaults.geometry",
            "Exactly one geometry must be enabled by default; enabled geometries: "
            + (", ".join(sorted(visible_geometry_ids)) or "none"),
        )
    if not extent_layers:
        report.add("error", "geometry.extent", "No API-derived Model Extents layer is published.")
    for geometry_id in geometry_ids:
        matches = [layer for layer in extent_layers.values() if layer.get("geometry") == geometry_id]
        if not matches:
            report.add(
                "error",
                "geometry.extent",
                f"Geometry {geometry_id} has no Model Extents layer.",
                geometry_id,
            )
    if extent_layers and not any(layer.get("visible") is True for layer in extent_layers.values()):
        report.add("error", "defaults.extent", "Model Extents must be enabled by default.")
    for layer_id, layer in extent_layers.items():
        if not _valid_wgs84_bounds(layer.get("bounds")):
            report.add("error", "geometry.extent-bounds", "Model Extents has invalid WGS84 bounds.", layer_id)

    plan_ids = sorted(
        {
            str(layer.get("plan"))
            for layer in layers.values()
            if layer.get("plan")
        }
    )
    raw_layers = {
        layer_id: layer for layer_id, layer in layers.items()
        if layer.get("sourceKind") == "raw-hdf"
    }
    stored_layers = {
        layer_id: layer for layer_id, layer in layers.items()
        if layer.get("sourceKind") == "stored-map"
    }
    calculated_layers = {
        layer_id: layer for layer_id, layer in layers.items()
        if layer.get("sourceKind") == "calculated"
    }
    terrain_layers = {
        layer_id: layer for layer_id, layer in layers.items()
        if layer.get("sourceKind") == "terrain"
    }
    for layer_id, layer in {**raw_layers, **stored_layers}.items():
        missing_titles = [
            key
            for key in ("planTitle", "geometryTitle")
            if not str(layer.get(key) or "").strip()
        ]
        if missing_titles:
            report.add(
                "error",
                "results.metadata",
                "Result layer is missing " + ", ".join(missing_titles) + ".",
                layer_id,
            )
        if layer.get("visible") is True:
            report.add(
                "error",
                "defaults.results",
                "Result layers must be disabled by default.",
                layer_id,
            )
    if not plan_ids:
        report.add("error", "results.plan", "No result plan is published.")
    admission_plan_ids = sorted(set(plan_ids) | completed_plan_ids)
    geometry_2d_ids = {
        str(layer.get("geometry"))
        for layer in geometry_layers.values()
        if layer.get("role") in _TWO_DIMENSIONAL_ROLES and layer.get("geometry")
    }
    archive_plans = {
        str(plan.get("plan_id")): plan
        for plan in (archive or {}).get("results", [])
        if isinstance(plan, Mapping) and plan.get("plan_id")
    }
    stored_map_exempt_plans: set[str] = set()
    for plan_id in admission_plan_ids:
        plan_raw = [layer for layer in raw_layers.values() if layer.get("plan") == plan_id]
        plan_stored = [layer for layer in stored_layers.values() if layer.get("plan") == plan_id]
        if not plan_raw:
            report.add(
                "error",
                "results.raw-hdf",
                "No raw HDF vector result layers are published.",
                plan_id,
            )
        expected_variables = _mappable_archive_variables(archive_plans.get(plan_id, {}))
        published_variables = {
            str((layer.get("provenance") or {}).get("variable") or "").casefold()
            for layer in plan_raw
            if (layer.get("provenance") or {}).get("variable")
        }
        for normalized_name, variable_name in expected_variables.items():
            if normalized_name not in published_variables:
                report.add(
                    "error",
                    "results.raw-variable",
                    f"Joinable raw HDF result variable {variable_name} is not published.",
                    f"{plan_id}:{variable_name}",
                )
        plan_geometry = str(archive_plans.get(plan_id, {}).get("geom_id") or "")
        stored_maps_applicable = bool(terrain_layers) or (
            plan_geometry in geometry_2d_ids
            if plan_geometry
            else bool(geometry_2d_ids)
        )
        if not plan_stored and stored_maps_applicable:
            report.add(
                "error",
                "results.stored-map",
                "No RASMapper Stored Map rasters are published.",
                plan_id,
            )
        elif not plan_stored:
            stored_map_exempt_plans.add(plan_id)
            report.add(
                "warning",
                "results.stored-map-not-applicable",
                "Pure 1D plan has no project terrain; continuous RASMapper Stored Map rasters are not applicable.",
                plan_id,
            )
        elif stored_maps_applicable:
            published_map_types = {
                map_type
                for layer in plan_stored
                if (
                    map_type := stored_map_type_key(
                        str((layer.get("provenance") or {}).get("mapType") or layer.get("role") or "")
                    )
                )
            }
            if any(
                _is_authoritative_depth_derived_boundary(layer)
                for layer in calculated_layers.values()
                if layer.get("plan") == plan_id
            ):
                published_map_types.add("inundation_boundary")
            missing_map_types = sorted(
                REQUIRED_STORED_MAP_TYPE_KEYS - published_map_types
            )
            if missing_map_types:
                report.add(
                    "error",
                    "results.stored-map-type",
                    "Complete Stored Map set is missing: "
                    + ", ".join(missing_map_types),
                    plan_id,
                )

    for layer_id, layer in raw_layers.items():
        query = layer.get("query") or {}
        provenance = layer.get("provenance") or {}
        if query.get("enabled") is not True:
            report.add("error", "results.raw-query", "Raw HDF layer is not queryable.", layer_id)
        if provenance.get("interpolationAuthority") != "none":
            report.add(
                "error",
                "results.raw-provenance",
                "Raw HDF values must explicitly declare no interpolation authority.",
                layer_id,
            )

    for layer_id, layer in stored_layers.items():
        query = layer.get("query") or {}
        provenance = layer.get("provenance") or {}
        numeric_id = query.get("numericResource")
        display_resource = resources.get(layer.get("resource")) or {}
        is_vector_stored_map = display_resource.get("type") == "vector-pmtiles"
        if (
            not is_vector_stored_map
            and (not numeric_id or (resources.get(numeric_id) or {}).get("type") != "cog")
        ):
            report.add(
                "error",
                "results.numeric-cog",
                "Stored Map has no authoritative numeric COG resource.",
                layer_id,
            )
        if is_vector_stored_map and query.get("enabled") is not True:
            report.add(
                "error",
                "results.vector-query",
                "Vector Stored Map is not queryable.",
                layer_id,
            )
        if provenance.get("interpolationAuthority") != "RASMapper/RasProcess":
            report.add(
                "error",
                "results.stored-provenance",
                "Stored Map must identify RASMapper/RasProcess as interpolation authority.",
                layer_id,
            )

    has_2d = any(layer.get("role") in _TWO_DIMENSIONAL_ROLES for layer in geometry_layers.values())
    if has_2d and not terrain_layers:
        report.add("error", "terrain.required", "A 2D model has no published terrain layer.")
    if has_2d and terrain_layers and not any(layer.get("visible") is True for layer in terrain_layers.values()):
        report.add("error", "defaults.terrain", "A 2D project terrain must be enabled by default.")
    for layer_id, layer in terrain_layers.items():
        query = layer.get("query") or {}
        numeric_id = query.get("numericResource")
        if not numeric_id or (resources.get(numeric_id) or {}).get("type") != "cog":
            report.add(
                "error",
                "terrain.numeric-cog",
                "Terrain has no associated queryable numeric COG.",
                layer_id,
            )

    basemap = next(
        (layer for layer in layers.values() if layer.get("role") == "basemap"),
        None,
    )
    if not basemap or basemap.get("visible") is not True:
        report.add("error", "defaults.basemap", "Hybrid satellite imagery must be enabled by default.")

    if archive is None:
        report.add(
            "error",
            "archive.required",
            "The archive manifest is required to verify successful plan completion.",
        )
    else:
        if not completed_plan_ids:
            report.add("error", "results.completed", "No successfully computed plan is recorded.")
        for plan_id in plan_ids:
            if plan_id not in completed_plan_ids:
                report.add(
                    "error",
                    "results.completed",
                    "Published result plan is not recorded as successfully computed.",
                    plan_id,
                )
        if terrain_layers:
            _validate_archive_terrain_policy(
                archive,
                report,
                base_dir=archive_path.parent if archive_path else None,
                check_files=check_files,
            )

    model_bounds = [layer.get("bounds") for layer in extent_layers.values() if _valid_wgs84_bounds(layer.get("bounds"))]
    numeric_stored_layers = {
        layer_id: layer
        for layer_id, layer in stored_layers.items()
        if (layer.get("query") or {}).get("numericResource")
    }
    for layer_id, layer in {**terrain_layers, **numeric_stored_layers}.items():
        numeric_id = (layer.get("query") or {}).get("numericResource")
        numeric = resources.get(numeric_id) or {}
        if not numeric.get("crs"):
            report.add("error", "raster.crs", "Numeric COG has no source CRS metadata.", layer_id)
        bounds = numeric.get("bounds")
        if not _valid_wgs84_bounds(bounds):
            report.add("error", "raster.bounds", "Numeric COG has invalid WGS84 bounds.", layer_id)
        elif model_bounds and not any(_bounds_intersect(bounds, extent) for extent in model_bounds):
            report.add("error", "raster.location", "Numeric COG does not intersect Model Extents.", layer_id)

    report.counts = {
        "resources": len(resources),
        "layers": len(layers),
        "geometries": len(geometry_ids),
        "plans": len(plan_ids),
        "completed_plans": len(completed_plan_ids),
        "raw_results": len(raw_layers),
        "stored_maps": len(stored_layers),
        "stored_map_exempt_plans": len(stored_map_exempt_plans),
        "terrains": len(terrain_layers),
    }
    return report

docs.title: mapping
docs.text: Result raster generation for HEC-RAS projects using the RASMapper engine.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
The mapping module generates georeferenced raster files (GeoTIFF) from completed HEC-RAS plan results. It uses a private compatibility adapter around ras-commander's stored-map APIs so profile selection is explicit and validated before map generation mutates the project.

Max and Min remain explicit summary selections. An exact named steady profile is resolved from the plan HDF and sent through RasMap.store_all_maps(mode="steady_profiles"); a missing or duplicate name raises an error instead of silently producing Max. Unsteady timestamps are likewise validated exactly. Whole-simulation products such as arrival time are generated separately because they do not have a profile dimension.

On Linux, RasProcess.exe runs under Wine. See the Linux/Wine Setup guide.

docs.title: Supported Map Types
docs.text:
Map Type CLI Flag Default Description wse --wse/--no-wse On Water Surface Elevation depth --depth/--no-depth On Depth velocity --velocity/--no-velocity On Velocity froude --froude Off Froude Number shear_stress --shear-stress Off Shear Stress depth_x_velocity --dv Off Depth x Velocity depth_x_velocity_sq --dv-sq Off Depth x Velocity² inundation_boundary --inundation-boundary Off Inundation Boundary (GeoJSON from the default fast-map engine, much faster; shapefile from RAS Mapper) arrival_time --arrival-time Off Arrival Time (hours, whole-simulation) duration --duration Off Inundation Duration (hours, whole-simulation) percent_inundated --percent-inundated Off Percent Time Inundated (whole-simulation)

--recession is accepted for compatibility but ignored with a warning — RasMapperLib has no recession map type, and only RasMapperLib-native outputs are produced.

docs.title: Whole-simulation map types
docs.text:
arrival_time, duration, and percent_inundated are computed over the entire simulation — the --profile option does not apply to them. Their filenames carry the --arrival-depth wet/dry threshold instead of the profile name, e.g. Arrival Time (0.1ft hrs).tif. They work with any ras-commander version: newer versions generate them natively via store_maps(); on older versions ras2cng pre-injects the stored-map entries into the .rasmap (restored afterwards) so the same StoreAllMaps run produces them.

Generating these types causes RasMapperLib to build a PostProcessing.hdf cache that can exceed the plan HDF in size; ras2cng deletes it from the output directory unless --keep-postprocessing is passed.

docs.title: Local performance policy
docs.text:
The default DEFAULT_LOCAL_MAP_PERFORMANCE preset is tuned for local processing on the 8-core, 31.8 GiB development workstation:

  • memory-aware automatic helper selection (max_workers=None);
  • enforced memory admission with an 8192 MiB / 25 percent reserve;
  • one GDAL thread per helper to prevent nested oversubscription;
  • a 64 MiB GDAL cache cap charged to every helper's memory estimate.

Only independent WSE, Depth, and Velocity products run concurrently. Large terrain estimates and products that require shared ordered state automatically use one helper. On the Spring River fixture, the measured estimate is about 11.2 GiB per helper, so this 31.8 GiB machine remains serial; a machine with more available memory can admit two or three map helpers without changing the call.

Use --map-workers 1 for a controlled serial comparison, or set the helper ceiling, reserve, and cache explicitly:

ras2cng map model.prj ./maps \
  --map-workers 2 \
  --map-reserve-memory-mb 8192 \
  --map-gdal-cache-mb 64

Python callers can provide the full typed policy without adding a second map function:

from ras_commander import StoreMapPerformanceOptions
from ras2cng import generate_result_maps

results = generate_result_maps(
    "model.prj",
    "maps",
    performance=StoreMapPerformanceOptions(
        max_workers=None,
        reserve_memory_mb=8192,
        gdal_cachemax_mb=64,
    ),
)

docs.title: Render Mode
docs.text:
The --render-mode option controls how the water surface is rendered to raster grids. This is critical for pixel-perfect output — HEC-RAS 6.x's RasProcess.exe ignores the render mode from the .rasmap file, so ras-commander uses RasStoreMapHelper.exe to set the mode explicitly before generating maps.

Mode Flag Description horizontal --render-mode horizontal Flat water surface within each mesh cell (default) sloping --render-mode sloping Interpolated sloping water surface slopingPretty --render-mode slopingPretty Sloping with depth-weighted face reduction (HEC-RAS 6.4+)

If --render-mode is not specified, the mode is read from the project's .rasmap file (defaults to horizontal if not set).

# Generate maps with sloping render mode
ras2cng map /path/to/project /output/maps --render-mode sloping

# Archive with slopingPretty render mode (requires HEC-RAS 6.4+)
ras2cng archive /path/to/project ./archive/ --results --map --render-mode slopingPretty

docs.title: Mapping engine: RAS Mapper or fast-map
docs.text:
fast-map is the default engine. It maps selected products through the Rust ras-commander-fast-map engine and hands everything else to RAS Mapper (RasStoreMapHelper.exe) per product group, printing the reason; --engine rasmapper (or RAS2CNG_MAP_ENGINE=rasmapper) renders every product through RAS Mapper. The water-surface render mode comes from the project's .rasmap, as RAS Mapper takes it (--render-mode overrides it); a project with no stored mode goes to RAS Mapper, which applies its own default. fast-map is built for FIM library creation on pure 2D models, not for general use across all model types: every fast-map product is qualified against RAS Mapper output (pixel conformance against native HEC-RAS 7.0.1 stored maps on the named models), and everything else falls back to RAS Mapper. ras-commander installs the engine through ras-commander[full] on Windows x64 and Linux x64 (ras2cng[fast-map] requests it explicitly). The mapping arithmetic needs no GDAL, and with the source-terrain path below no HEC-RAS either.

# Default: Rust WSE/Depth, arrival time and percent inundated; the rest via RAS Mapper
ras2cng map /path/to/project /output/maps \
    --arrival-time --percent-inundated --arrival-depth 0.5 --ras-version 7.0.1

# Everything through RAS Mapper
ras2cng map /path/to/project /output/maps --engine rasmapper

# Reuse a terrain export across runs
ras2cng map /path/to/project /output/maps --engine fast-map \
    --fast-map-terrain /output/maps/_fast_map_terrain/Terrain50.tif

# Fail instead of falling back (qualification runs)
ras2cng map /path/to/project /output/maps --engine fast-map --fast-map-strict

# Map a plan with storage areas in Rust (opt-in; otherwise RAS Mapper maps it)
ras2cng map /path/to/project /output/maps --fast-map-storage-areas

RAS2CNG_MAP_ENGINE selects the engine everywhere, including ras2cng archive --map. Scope, engine and render mode are checked from the plan HDF and .rasmap before any terrain work, so an out-of-scope plan goes to RAS Mapper without a terrain export.

Product fast-map Qualification against RAS Mapper WSE, Depth (Max) yes identical float32 values and masks on five models (1.2–3.6× faster for horizontal and plain sloping, 1.8–7.3× for depth-weighted sloping faces; evidence); Davis p02 and Bald Eagle bridges p05 again on the source-terrain path WSE, Depth with storage areas opt-in (--fast-map-storage-areas; slower than RAS Mapper today), as RAS Mapper level pools, when the engine advertises storage-area-level-pool/1 identical on Bald Eagle p07 and p04 in every render mode (466,912 / 461,639 storage-area px); p07 Max sloping through ras2cng map: 0 mask and 0 bit differences on 1,345,691 px Arrival time, percent time inundated yes (--no-fast-map-whole-simulation to opt out) identical on Davis p02 (4,879 px) and bridges p05 (959,043 px) at 0.5 ft, horizontal and plain sloping; with a storage area, p07 (1,333,183 px) Duration yes, when the engine advertises RAS Mapper's recession rule (rasmapper-backward-window-recession/1); not with storage areas identical on Davis p02 and bridges p05 at 0.5 ft Velocity (Max) yes in plain sloping and horizontal when the engine advertises velocity_depth; slopingPretty opt-in (--fast-map-velocity); --no-fast-map-velocity to opt out; not with storage areas bridges p05: 0 value and 0 mask differences in sloping (973,902 px) and horizontal (973,532 px). slopingPretty: identical values on every common pixel, but its mask follows the slopingPretty depth, which differs on bridges Max (75 + 28 px). Older engines: opt-in, plain sloping only D × V, D × V², Froude (Max) yes in plain sloping and horizontal (--no-fast-map-derived to opt out); not with storage areas or slopingPretty per-time product, pixelwise Max over every output time, as RAS Mapper computes it: 0 / 0 on bridges p05 over 433 times (973,956 px sloping); Davis within 2 ulp on ≤ 5 px Shear stress no not implemented in the engine Inundation boundary yes (see below); not with storage areas deterministic contours, not vector parity

A plan is sent to RAS Mapper instead when:

Condition Why 1D river reaches or cross sections Outside the engine's method (RasFim.validate_2d_model) Storage areas, unless --fast-map-storage-areas (fast_map_storage_areas=True, RAS2CNG_FAST_MAP_STORAGE_AREAS=1) is given Not a default until it is faster than RAS Mapper: Bald Eagle p07 WSE + Depth took 18.7 s in Rust against 12.2 s. Opt in to map storage-area plans without HEC-RAS (Linux, FIM batches) Storage areas, opted in, with an engine that does not advertise storage-area-level-pool/1 It would leave the storage-area pixels blank A profile other than Max (per-profile products only; arrival, duration and percent are whole-simulation) Timestep mapping is not wired through ras2cng yet. Decided before any terrain work No usable terrain See below Engine missing or failed No arithmetic fallback inside fast-map

Terrain. With ras-commander's RasFim.top_priority_terrain_source (ras-commander #724, fast-map #11), ras2cng maps on the terrain's unmodified priority-1 source TIFF, with its terrain-HDF footprint mask, and skips the RAS Mapper terrain export. Inside that footprint the source TIFF is the effective terrain, and the engine refuses when a wet cell would draw outside it. ras2cng then:

  1. retries on the source's CRS-canonical copy, only when the refusal was about the CRS (Davis);
  2. otherwise builds the native effective terrain once per run, when the engine advertises rasmapper-effective-terrain/1 and RasFim has build_effective_terrain: RAS Mapper's multi-source mosaic (stitch TIN first, then each source in priority order) rebuilt in Rust from the source TIFFs, their level-0 masks and the stitch TIN, without HEC-RAS. On Bald Eagle Terrain50 the valid mask is identical on 197,179,058 px and 8 values differ, all in stitch-TIN corners where RAS Mapper's own exports disagree (max 1.53 ft); it took 7.0 s and 1.4 GB, against about 190 s for the export. Terrains with modifications are refused;
  3. otherwise exports the plan's terrain once per run through RAS Mapper (RasTerrain.export_rasmapper_terrain, HEC-RAS 6.4.1/6.5/6.6/7.0.1/7.1; pass --ras-version).

--fast-map-terrain supplies a float32 export (with modifications) instead, --no-fast-map-effective-terrain skips step 2, and --no-fast-map-source-terrain skips the source TIFF.

Terrains with modifications always go to RAS Mapper. Before any of the steps above, ras2cng reads the terrain HDF's /Modifications group and the .rasmap's modification layers (ras2cng.terrain.terrain_modifications). If it finds any, or cannot read the terrain HDF, steps 1 and 2 are skipped and RAS Mapper's export builds the terrain (step 3), and the inundation boundary is drawn by RAS Mapper. Rust terrain operations run only on unmodified terrains, even with an engine build that accepts modifications: that work is parked because it does not yet reproduce RAS Mapper on real modified terrains. map-hdf with a single raw --terrain TIFF passes that TIFF directly.

Measured on a shared, loaded host:

Run Time Terrain Bald Eagle bridges p05, WSE + Depth 4.5 s end to end, no HEC-RAS priority-1 source TIFF bridges p05, WSE, Depth, velocity, arrival, percent 16.6 s reused export bridges p05, same five, nothing supplied 181 s (≈160 s is the HEC-RAS export; arrival/percent were refused on the source) source, then export RAS Mapper, bridges p05 ≈215 s for the seven Max products; ≈26 s for arrival/percent Davis p02, all five 5.4 s, no HEC-RAS CRS-canonical source copy bridges p05 sloping, nine products (adds velocity, D × V, D × V², Froude, duration) 251 s / 1.5 GB with one output time in flight in the derived pass; the derived pass alone is now 141 s / 2.6 GB source; effective terrain for arrival/duration/percent RAS Mapper, the same nine 235 s / 2.4 GB; derived only 206 s / 2.3 GB; the other six 34 s fast-map, the other six 25 s / 1.5 GB source and effective Bald Eagle p07 (storage area), WSE + Depth 18.7 s / 1.5 GB (RAS Mapper: 12.2 s / 1.2 GB) native effective terrain (the source TIFF is refused: 28 storage-area pixels outside it) p07, arrival + percent 31 s (RAS Mapper: 82 s) native effective terrain

Every fast-map product in the bridges and p07 rows was compared with RAS Mapper 7.0.1 stored maps: 0 mask and 0 bit differences (bridges: 18 products over sloping and horizontal; p07: 1,345,691 and 1,333,183 px).

Output. Products are named like RAS Mapper's (WSE (Max).tif, Depth (Max).tif, Velocity (Max).tif, D _ V (Max).tif, D _ V^2 (Max).tif, Froude (Max).tif, Arrival Time (0.5ft hrs).tif, Duration (0.5ft hrs).tif, Percent Time Inundated (0.5ft).tif) on the terrain's pixel grid, with NaN nodata, next to fast_map_manifest.json, fast_map_velocity_manifest.json, fast_map_derived_manifest.json and fast_map_whole_simulation_manifest.json (engine version, method, terrain, storage areas, timings). Arrival time is in hours since the simulation start. MapResult.engines records which engine produced each map type, MapResult.fast_map_skipped why a map type went to RAS Mapper under the fast-map engine (for example storage areas without the opt-in), and MapResult.fast_map_terrain which terrain fast-map used (source, source-canonical, effective, export or supplied). Velocity is its own engine call, so a velocity refusal never costs WSE/Depth, and WSE/Depth keep the native GeoTIFF writer; in horizontal mode it is rendered plain sloping and clipped with the horizontal depth, as RAS Mapper does. --min-depth, --wgs84 and --cog apply unchanged. Other options: --fast-map-threads (default CPUs − 1) and --fast-map-memory-mib (planned working memory; default a quarter of RAM, 1–16 GiB).

Invalid cell polygons. HEC-RAS can compute 2D cells whose face polylines cross. With ras-commander 0.110.2 or newer, fast-map maps those meshes under an explicit policy instead of refusing them:

--fast-map-invalid-cells Pixel ownership of an invalid cell repair (engine default) polygonize the cell's faces, remove area owned by valid cells, keep the largest part hull the face-point convex hull, with the same overlap removal omit the cell owns no pixels raise refuse; the products fall back to RAS Mapper (--fast-map-strict raises)

Hydraulic connectivity and interpolation always use the complete HDF topology; only pixel ownership changes. RAS Mapper's own rendering of such cells has not been qualified against repair. Every affected cell (mesh, cell id, reason, action, original and mapped area) is recorded as fim-invalid-cells/1 in MapResult.invalid_cells, fast_map_manifest.json and fast_map_whole_simulation_manifest.json, and a non-zero count is printed.

GeoTIFF delivery. With ras-commander-fast-map 0.11 the engine writes the sloping WSE/Depth GeoTIFFs itself (terrio, LZW) instead of handing float32 arrays back to Python for rasterio. --fast-map-writer auto (default) uses it when the engine supports it and velocity is not requested; native requires it and rasterio keeps the previous path (RAS2CNG_FAST_MAP_WRITER sets the default). On Bald Eagle bridges p05 Max the two writers gave identical pixels and the same LZW strip layout; native files were about 4% smaller and the engine call used about 18% less peak memory. --cog converts either through the shared COG policy with identical results. MapResult.fast_map_writer records the writer.

docs.title: Inundation boundaries in Rust (recommended with fast-map)
docs.text:
RAS Mapper's inundation-boundary export is very slow. With fast-map (the default engine), --inundation-boundary is mapped by the Rust engine (RasFim.map_inundation_boundaries) whenever the plan is in scope. In ras-commander's Davis pipes/conduits comparison, the Rust batch for Max plus one timestep took 3.5 s against 85 s for the two native RAS Mapper calls. It is not the default engine, but it is the recommended way to produce boundaries for pure 2D models.

# Rust WSE/Depth and boundary; velocity still through RAS Mapper
ras2cng map /path/to/project /output/maps --engine fast-map --inundation-boundary

# Explicit single-source terrain HDF (its TIFF is found beside it)
ras2cng map /path/to/project /output/maps --engine fast-map --inundation-boundary \
    --fast-map-terrain-hdf /path/to/project/Terrain/Terrain.hdf

# Keep boundaries on RAS Mapper while still using Rust rasters
ras2cng map /path/to/project /output/maps --engine fast-map --inundation-boundary \
    --no-fast-map-boundary

It is a different method, not a copy of RAS Mapper's polygons. The Rust engine traces deterministic zero-depth contours (deterministic-zero-depth-contours/1): the same inputs always give byte-identical GeoJSON, on Windows and Linux and at any worker count. RAS Mapper's own boundary polygons are order-dependent and can differ between identical exports, so the two are close but not equal. On Davis Max the Rust contour had 66 holes and 47,426 vertices, against RAS Mapper's 65 and 47,396. Almost all of the 7,423 ft² difference was one hole that RAS Mapper filled. The Depth/WSE rasters are unaffected; they still match RAS Mapper bit for bit.

Extra scope for boundaries, on top of the pure-2D rules above (each falls back to RAS Mapper on its own, so the rasters can still use Rust):

Condition Why Terrain with more than one source TIFF The method needs the original terrain HDF's masks, perimeters and stitch TIN for a single source. The flattened raster export cannot stand in for them Terrain modifications Refused by ras2cng before the engine runs (terrain_modifications): modified terrains always go to RAS Mapper slopingPretty render mode Contours support horizontal and plain sloping only ras-commander without RasFim.map_inundation_boundaries Needs ras-commander 0.113.0 Storage areas The contour method draws 2D cells only; the level pool would be missing A terrain CRS the engine and rasterio read differently (Davis), without --fast-map-terrain-crs-hash The engine cannot name an EPSG code for it; ras2cng never guesses the identity (see below)

User-supplied terrain CRS. When the engine cannot name the terrain's EPSG code and reads its WKT differently from rasterio (Davis), the boundary falls back to RAS Mapper, and the message prints the engine's WKT hash, for example:

engine terrain CRS differs from rasterio CRS EPSG:2871; the engine reports
crs_wkt_fnv1a64=e446f7bd6bdb4d7f for Terrain (1).Davis_terrain2.tif ...

Check the CRS first (ras2fim-batch terrain-info <terrain.tif> prints the engine's WKT and crs_wkt_fnv1a64), then pass the hash:

ras2cng map /path/to/Davis /output/maps --inundation-boundary \
    --fast-map-terrain-crs-hash e446f7bd6bdb4d7f

The Python API takes fast_map_terrain_crs_fnv1a64=. It applies to the boundary terrain only, is used only when the engine reports no EPSG code, and a value that does not equal the engine's hash is refused. The boundary manifest records it as ras2cng.terrain_crs_fnv1a64.

Output. Inundation Boundary (Max).geojson: a MultiPolygon with holes, in the model CRS. RAS Mapper writes a shapefile. It sits next to fast_map_boundary_manifest.json, which records the method, polygon/hole/vertex counts, area, terrain and timings. A plan with no flooded area writes no boundary.

docs.title: Post-Processing Options
docs.text:
• Minimum depth threshold (--min-depth): Set pixels below a depth threshold to NoData
  • WGS84 reprojection (--wgs84): Reproject output rasters to EPSG:4326 using rasterio
  • Cloud Optimized GeoTIFF (--cog): Convert output to COG using gdal_translate

@dataclass
class MapResult:
    """Result of map generation for a single plan."""
    plan_id: str
    plan_number: str
    map_types: dict[str, list[Path]] = field(default_factory=dict)  # {"depth": [Path(...)]}
    output_dir: Path = field(default_factory=lambda: Path("."))
    errors: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    # Engine that produced each map type: "rasmapper" or "fast-map".
    engines: dict[str, str] = field(default_factory=dict)
    # For fast-map products, the terrain the engine mapped on: "supplied"
    # (--fast-map-terrain), "source" (the priority-1 terrain source TIFF, no
    # export), "source-canonical" (its CRS-canonical copy) or "export" (the
    # RAS Mapper terrain export).
    fast_map_terrain: dict[str, str] = field(default_factory=dict)
    # For fast-map products, the engine's ``fim-invalid-cells/1`` record
    # (ras-commander 0.110.2+): the policy, the count and every cell whose
    # face polylines do not form a valid polygon, with the action taken.
    # Absent for map types RAS Mapper produced or older ras-commander.
    invalid_cells: dict[str, dict] = field(default_factory=dict)
    # For fast-map sloping WSE/Depth/velocity, how the GeoTIFFs were written:
    # "native" (terrio LZW, in the engine) or "rasterio".
    fast_map_writer: dict[str, str] = field(default_factory=dict)
    # With the fast-map engine, why a map type went to RAS Mapper instead
    # (e.g. storage areas without --fast-map-storage-areas, 1D elements, a
    # non-Max profile). Empty under --engine rasmapper.
    fast_map_skipped: dict[str, str] = field(default_factory=dict)

None map_engine Optional[str]

"fast-map" (default) maps, on pure 2D models, the products the Rust ras-commander-fast-map engine is qualified for against RAS Mapper stored maps (Max WSE/Depth, velocity, D x V, D x V², Froude, arrival time, percent inundated, duration, each as far as the installed engine advertises it; storage areas as level pools) and the inundation boundary through deterministic contours (much faster than RAS Mapper's export; close to, not identical with, its polygons). It is built for FIM library creation, not every model type: 1D elements, shear stress, other profiles and unqualified render modes fall back to RAS Mapper per product group. "rasmapper" renders every map type through RAS Mapper. None reads RAS2CNG_MAP_ENGINE, else fast_map.DEFAULT_MAP_ENGINE. The render mode comes from the project's .rasmap unless render_mode is given. None fast_map_memory_mib Optional[int]

True fast_map_terrain_hdf Optional[Path]

Original single-source terrain HDF for Rust boundaries; its TIFF is found beside it. None uses the plan's terrain (or terrain_name).

None fast_map_source_terrain bool

With fast-map and no fast_map_terrain, map on the terrain's priority-1 source TIFF first, skipping the RAS Mapper terrain export, and export only when the engine refuses (a wet cell draws outside that source's footprint). Needs ras-commander with RasFim.top_priority_terrain_source.

True fast_map_whole_simulation bool

With fast-map, also map arrival_time and percent_inundated in Rust (threshold arrival_depth; horizontal and plain sloping), and duration when the engine advertises RAS Mapper's recession rule (fast-map

True fast_map_velocity Optional[bool]

None (default): map Max velocity in Rust in plain sloping and horizontal mode when the engine has the fast-map #20 velocity rules (0 value / 0 mask differences on bridges p05). True also maps slopingPretty velocity (opt-in: its mask follows the slopingPretty depth, which differs from RAS Mapper's on bridges Max) and plain sloping on older engines. False leaves velocity to RAS Mapper.

None fast_map_derived bool

With fast-map, map Max D x V, D x V² and Froude in Rust (one time-series pass, reduce_max/1) in plain sloping and horizontal mode. False leaves them to RAS Mapper.

True fast_map_effective_terrain bool

Before exporting the terrain through RAS Mapper, try RAS Mapper's effective terrain rebuilt in Rust (fast-map #19; unmodified terrains only). False skips it.

True fast_map_storage_areas Optional[bool]

Opt-in: it is slower than RAS Mapper today (p07 WSE + Depth 18.7 s vs 12.2 s), so by default (None reads RAS2CNG_FAST_MAP_STORAGE_AREAS, else off) such plans go wholly to RAS Mapper, and MapResult.fast_map_skipped says why. Use it to map storage-area plans without HEC-RAS (Linux, FIM batches).

For Rust inundation boundaries only: the engine's WKT hash (crs_wkt_fnv1a64) of the boundary terrain TIFF, accepted when the engine cannot identify the terrain's EPSG code and its CRS reads differently from rasterio's (e.g. Davis). ras2cng never guesses it: obtain it with ras2fim-batch terrain-info <terrain.tif> (or from the refusal message, which prints it), check the CRS is right, and pass it. A mismatch with the engine's hash is refused.

None fast_map_invalid_cells Optional[str]

Pixel ownership for 2D cells whose face polylines do not form a valid polygon: "repair" (the engine default), "hull", "omit" or "raise" (refuse, so the products fall back to RAS Mapper). None fast_map_fallback bool

When a plan is outside fast-map's scope (1D elements, a non-Max profile, no usable terrain, engine missing or failed), render it through RAS Mapper instead. False raises.

True

            is slower than RAS Mapper today (p07 WSE + Depth 18.7 s vs
            12.2 s), so by default (``None`` reads
            ``RAS2CNG_FAST_MAP_STORAGE_AREAS``, else off) such plans go wholly
            to RAS Mapper, and ``MapResult.fast_map_skipped`` says why. Use it
            to map storage-area plans without HEC-RAS (Linux, FIM batches).
        fast_map_terrain_crs_fnv1a64: For Rust inundation boundaries only:
            the engine's WKT hash (``crs_wkt_fnv1a64``) of the boundary
            terrain TIFF, accepted when the engine cannot identify the
            terrain's EPSG code and its CRS reads differently from rasterio's
            (e.g. Davis). ras2cng never guesses it: obtain it with
            ``ras2fim-batch terrain-info <terrain.tif>`` (or from the refusal
            message, which prints it), check the CRS is right, and pass it.
            A mismatch with the engine's hash is refused.
        fast_map_invalid_cells: Pixel ownership for 2D cells whose face
            polylines do not form a valid polygon: ``"repair"`` (the engine
            default), ``"hull"``, ``"omit"`` or ``"raise"`` (refuse, so the
            products fall back to RAS Mapper). None keeps the engine default.
            Needs ras-commander 0.110.2+; the affected cells are recorded in
            ``MapResult.invalid_cells`` and the fast-map manifests.
        fast_map_writer: Sloping GeoTIFF delivery: ``"auto"`` (default;
            native terrio LZW when the engine supports it and velocity is not
            requested), ``"native"`` (required) or ``"rasterio"``. None reads
            ``RAS2CNG_FAST_MAP_WRITER``. Both give identical pixels and the
            same LZW strip layout; ``--cog`` still goes through
            :mod:`ras2cng.cog`.
        fast_map_fallback: When a plan is outside fast-map's scope (1D
            elements, a non-Max profile, no usable terrain, engine missing or
            failed), render it through RAS Mapper instead. False raises.

    Returns:
        List of MapResult, one per processed plan
    """
    from ras2cng import fast_map as _fast_map
    from ras2cng.project import resolve_project_path

    # Validate fast-map options before any project or engine work.
    fast_map_invalid_cells = _fast_map.normalize_invalid_cells(fast_map_invalid_cells)
    fast_map_writer = _fast_map.resolve_product_writer(fast_map_writer)
    fast_map_storage_areas = _fast_map.resolve_storage_areas(fast_map_storage_areas)
    fast_map_terrain_crs_fnv1a64 = _fast_map.normalize_crs_fnv1a64(
        fast_map_terrain_crs_fnv1a64
    )

    project_path = Path(project_path)
    # Absolute: RAS Mapper resolves a relative folder against the project, so
    # its rasters would land under the project instead of here.
    output_dir = Path(output_dir).resolve()
    output_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    project_dir, prj_file = resolve_project_path(project_path)

    console.print(f"\n[bold cyan]ras2cng map[/bold cyan] -> {output_dir}")
    console.print(f"  Project : {prj_file.name}")
    console.print(f"  Profile : {profile}")

    engine = _fast_map.resolve_map_engine(map_engine)
    terrain_resolver = None
    if engine == _fast_map.FAST_MAP:
        rust_products = ["WSE/Depth"]
        if fast_map_velocity is not False:
            rust_products.append("velocity")
        if fast_map_derived:
            rust_products.append("D x V/Froude (Max)")
        if fast_map_whole_simulation:
            rust_products.append("arrival time/percent inundated/duration")
        if fast_map_boundary:
            rust_products.append("inundation boundary")
        if fast_map_storage_areas:
            rust_products.append("storage areas (opt-in)")
        console.print(
            f"  Engine  : fast-map (Rust) for {', '.join(rust_products)} on pure 2D "
            "models (FIM library scope) where the installed engine is qualified; "
            "RAS Mapper for everything else"
        )
        terrain_resolver = _fast_map.TerrainResolver(
            prj_file,
            output_dir / "_fast_map_terrain",
            terrain_path=fast_map_terrain,
            terrain_name=terrain_name,
            ras_version=ras_version,
            terrain_hdf=fast_map_terrain_hdf,
            effective=fast_map_effective_terrain,
            threads=fast_map_threads,
            max_working_mib=fast_map_memory_mib,
        )
    else:
        console.print("  Engine  : RAS Mapper")

    optimized_store_maps = _supports_optimized_store_maps()
    if performance is not None and not optimized_store_maps:
        raise RuntimeError(
            "performance requires ras-commander>=0.99.0; upgrade ras-commander "
            "or omit performance to use the serial compatibility path"
        )
    if performance is not None:
        effective_performance = performance
    elif optimized_store_maps:
        effective_performance = DEFAULT_LOCAL_MAP_PERFORMANCE
    else:
        effective_performance = None
    if effective_performance is not None:
        worker_label = (
            "auto"
            if effective_performance.max_workers is None
            else str(effective_performance.max_workers)
        )
        console.print(
            f"  Mapping : {worker_label} helper(s), "
            f"{effective_performance.memory_policy} memory admission"
        )
    else:
        console.print("  Mapping : serial compatibility path")

    # Configure RasProcess
    _configure_rasprocess(rasprocess_path, ras_version)

    # Initialize project (pass ras_version to avoid auto-detecting old versions from plan files)
    init_kwargs = dict(ras_object="new", load_results_summary=True)
    if ras_version:
        init_kwargs["ras_version"] = ras_version
    ras = init_ras_project(project_dir, **init_kwargs)
    if rasprocess_path:
        exe_path = Path(rasprocess_path)
        ras.ras_exe_path = str(
            exe_path
            if exe_path.suffix.lower() == ".exe"
            else exe_path / "RasProcess.exe"
        )

    # RasMapperLib has no recession MapType (verified 6.6/7.0.1) — only
    # RasMapperLib-native products are generated.
    if recession:
        console.print(
            "  [yellow]Warning:[/yellow] recession has no RasMapperLib map type "
            "- skipping (arrival_time and duration are available)"
        )
        recession = False

    # Build list of requested map types
    requested_types = _build_requested_types(
        wse=wse, depth=depth, velocity=velocity,
        froude=froude, shear_stress=shear_stress,
        depth_x_velocity=depth_x_velocity,
        depth_x_velocity_sq=depth_x_velocity_sq,
        inundation_boundary=inundation_boundary,
        arrival_time=arrival_time, duration=duration,
        percent_inundated=percent_inundated,
    )

    if not requested_types:
        console.print("[yellow]Warning:[/yellow] No map types selected")
        return []

    if "inundation_boundary" in requested_types and (reproject_wgs84 or convert_cog):
        console.print(
            "  [yellow]Note:[/yellow] raster post-processing (--wgs84/--cog) does "
            "not apply to the inundation boundary shapefile - it stays in the "
            "model CRS"
        )

    console.print(f"  Map types: {', '.join(requested_types)}")

    # Determine which plans to process
    plan_filter = set(plans) if plans else None
    plan_rows = ras.plan_df if ras.plan_df is not None and not ras.plan_df.empty else None

    if plan_rows is None:
        console.print("[yellow]Warning:[/yellow] No plans found in project")
        return []

    results: list[MapResult] = []

    for _, row in plan_rows.iterrows():
        plan_num = str(row.get("plan_number", "")).zfill(2)
        plan_id = f"p{plan_num}"

        if plan_filter and plan_id not in plan_filter:
            continue

        plan_hdf = project_dir / f"{ras.project_name}.p{plan_num}.hdf"
        if not plan_hdf.exists():
            console.print(f"  [{plan_id}] No HDF results - skipping")
            continue

        plan_output = output_dir / plan_id
        plan_output.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

        map_result = MapResult(
            plan_id=plan_id,
            plan_number=plan_num,
            output_dir=plan_output,
        )

        console.print(f"  [{plan_id}] Generating maps...")

        try:
            fast_results: dict[str, list[Path]] = {}
            fast_render = None
            if terrain_resolver is not None:
                # Scope, engine and render mode first: an out-of-scope plan
                # (1D, storage areas, no stored render mode) must not pay for
                # a terrain export before going to RAS Mapper.
                try:
                    fast_render = _fast_map.preflight(
                        plan_hdf, ras, render_mode, storage_areas=fast_map_storage_areas,
                    )
                except _fast_map.FastMapUnavailable as exc:
                    if not fast_map_fallback:
                        raise
                    console.print(
                        f"    [yellow]fast-map not used[/yellow] ({exc}); using RAS Mapper"
                    )
                    for map_type in requested_types:
                        map_result.fast_map_skipped[map_type] = str(exc)
            if fast_render is not None:
                # WSE/Depth and the boundary use different terrain inputs, so
                # each falls back to RAS Mapper on its own.
                def _fast_group(label, run, types=()):
                    try:
                        produced = run()
                    except Exception as exc:
                        if not fast_map_fallback:
                            raise
                        console.print(
                            f"    [yellow]fast-map {label} unavailable[/yellow] "
                            f"({exc}); using RAS Mapper"
                        )
                        for map_type in types:
                            if map_type in requested_types:
                                map_result.fast_map_skipped[map_type] = str(exc)
                        return {}
                    console.print(
                        f"    fast-map: {', '.join(produced)} mapped in Rust"
                    )
                    record = getattr(produced, "invalid_cells", None)
                    writer = getattr(produced, "product_writer", None)
                    for map_type in produced:
                        if record is not None:
                            map_result.invalid_cells[map_type] = record
                        if writer is not None:
                            map_result.fast_map_writer[map_type] = writer
                    if record and record.get("count"):
                        console.print(
                            f"    [yellow]fast-map {label}:[/yellow] {record['count']} invalid "
                            f"2D cell polygon(s) handled with invalid_cells="
                            f"{record.get('policy')!r} (see the fast-map manifest)"
                        )
                    return produced

                def _on_terrain(label, run):
                    """Run on the cheapest terrain the engine accepts; record it."""
                    notes_before = len(terrain_resolver.notes)
                    produced, kind = _fast_map.with_terrain(
                        terrain_resolver, plan_hdf, run, use_source=fast_map_source_terrain,
                    )
                    for note in terrain_resolver.notes[notes_before:]:
                        console.print(f"    fast-map {label}: {note}")
                    for map_type in produced:
                        map_result.fast_map_terrain[map_type] = kind
                    return produced

                def _skip(label, reason, *, strict=False, types=()):
                    """A product group outside fast-map's scope goes to RAS Mapper.

                    ``strict``: also refused under --fast-map-strict (as the
                    per-profile maps always were); qualification limits such
                    as slopingPretty velocity are not errors. ``types`` are
                    recorded in ``MapResult.fast_map_skipped``.
                    """
                    if strict and not fast_map_fallback:
                        raise _fast_map.FastMapUnavailable(f"{label}: {reason}")
                    for map_type in types:
                        if map_type in requested_types:
                            map_result.fast_map_skipped[map_type] = reason
                    console.print(
                        f"    [yellow]fast-map {label} not used[/yellow] ({reason}); "
                        "using RAS Mapper"
                    )

                # Per-profile products are Max only through fast-map. Decided
                # here, before any terrain work: inside with_terrain a refusal
                # reads as a terrain refusal and would cost an export.
                max_profile = profile == "Max"
                profile_reason = f"fast-map maps the Max profile only (got {profile!r})"
                if not max_profile and any(
                    t in requested_types
                    for t in (*_fast_map.FAST_MAP_RASTER_TYPES, "velocity",
                              *_fast_map.FAST_MAP_DERIVED_TYPES, _fast_map.FAST_MAP_BOUNDARY)
                ):
                    _skip("per-profile maps", profile_reason, strict=True, types=(
                        *_fast_map.FAST_MAP_RASTER_TYPES, "velocity",
                        *_fast_map.FAST_MAP_DERIVED_TYPES, _fast_map.FAST_MAP_BOUNDARY,
                    ))
                if max_profile and any(
                    t in _fast_map.FAST_MAP_RASTER_TYPES for t in requested_types
                ):
                    fast_results.update(_fast_group("WSE/Depth", lambda: _on_terrain(
                        "WSE/Depth",
                        lambda tif, hdf, kind: _fast_map.map_plan(
                            plan_hdf,
                            tif,
                            plan_output,
                            map_types=requested_types,
                            profile=profile,
                            render=fast_render,
                            threads=fast_map_threads,
                            timeout=timeout,
                            max_working_mib=fast_map_memory_mib,
                            terrain_hdf=hdf,
                            terrain_kind=kind,
                            invalid_cells=fast_map_invalid_cells,
                            product_writer=fast_map_writer,
                        ),
                    ), types=_fast_map.FAST_MAP_RASTER_TYPES))
                if max_profile and "velocity" in requested_types:
                    velocity_depth, reason = _fast_map.velocity_plan(
                        fast_render, fast_map_velocity
                    )
                    if reason is not None:
                        _skip("velocity", reason, types=("velocity",))
                    else:
                        fast_results.update(_fast_group("velocity", lambda: _on_terrain(
                            "velocity",
                            lambda tif, hdf, kind: _fast_map.map_velocity(
                                plan_hdf,
                                tif,
                                plan_output,
                                render=fast_render,
                                velocity_depth=velocity_depth,
                                profile=profile,
                                threads=fast_map_threads,
                                timeout=timeout,
                                max_working_mib=fast_map_memory_mib,
                                terrain_hdf=hdf,
                                terrain_kind=kind,
                                invalid_cells=fast_map_invalid_cells,
                            ),
                        ), types=("velocity",)))
                derived_types = [
                    t for t in _fast_map.FAST_MAP_DERIVED_TYPES if t in requested_types
                ]
                if max_profile and derived_types:
                    reason = _fast_map.derived_plan(fast_render, fast_map_derived)
                    if reason is not None:
                        _skip("D x V/Froude", reason, types=derived_types)
                    else:
                        fast_results.update(_fast_group("D x V/Froude", lambda: _on_terrain(
                            "D x V/Froude",
                            lambda tif, hdf, kind: _fast_map.map_derived(
                                plan_hdf,
                                tif,
                                plan_output,
                                map_types=derived_types,
                                render=fast_render,
                                profile=profile,
                                threads=fast_map_threads,
                                timeout=timeout,
                                max_working_mib=fast_map_memory_mib,
                                terrain_hdf=hdf,
                                terrain_kind=kind,
                                invalid_cells=fast_map_invalid_cells,
                            ),
                        ), types=derived_types))
                whole_types, whole_notes = _fast_map.whole_simulation_types(
                    requested_types, fast_render
                )
                for note in whole_notes if fast_map_whole_simulation else ():
                    _skip("whole simulation", note)
                if fast_map_whole_simulation and whole_types:
                    fast_results.update(_fast_group("whole simulation", lambda: _on_terrain(
                        "whole simulation",
                        lambda tif, hdf, kind: _fast_map.map_whole_simulation(
                            plan_hdf,
                            tif,
                            plan_output,
                            map_types=whole_types,
                            threshold=arrival_depth,
                            render=fast_render,
                            terrain_hdf=hdf,
                            threads=fast_map_threads,
                            timeout=timeout,
                            max_working_mib=fast_map_memory_mib,
                            terrain_kind=kind,
                            invalid_cells=fast_map_invalid_cells,
                        ),
                    ), types=whole_types))
                if (
                    max_profile and fast_map_boundary
                    and _fast_map.FAST_MAP_BOUNDARY in requested_types
                ):
                    def _boundary():
                        tif, terrain_hdf = terrain_resolver.boundary_terrain(plan_hdf)
                        return _fast_map.map_boundary(
                            plan_hdf, tif, terrain_hdf, plan_output,
                            profile=profile,
                            render=fast_render,
                            terrain_crs_fnv1a64=fast_map_terrain_crs_fnv1a64,
                            threads=fast_map_threads,
                            timeout=timeout,
                            max_working_mib=fast_map_memory_mib,
                            invalid_cells=fast_map_invalid_cells,
                        )
                    fast_results.update(_fast_group(
                        "inundation boundary", _boundary, types=(_fast_map.FAST_MAP_BOUNDARY,)
                    ))

            rasmapper_types = [t for t in requested_types if t not in fast_results]

            # Build boolean flags for RasProcess.store_maps()
            type_flags = {t: (t in rasmapper_types) for t in MAP_TYPE_VARIABLES}

            plan_run_started = time.time() - 2  # filesystem mtime slack

            result_dict: dict[str, list[Path]] = {}
            if rasmapper_types:
                result_dict = _generate_plan_maps(
                    ras=ras,
                    plan_number=plan_num,
                    profile=profile,
                    output_dir=plan_output,
                    terrain_name=terrain_name,
                    render_mode=render_mode,
                    timeout=timeout,
                    arrival_depth=arrival_depth,
                    ras_version=ras_version,
                    performance=effective_performance,
                    **type_flags,
                )
            for map_type in rasmapper_types:
                map_result.engines[map_type] = _fast_map.RASMAPPER
            for map_type, paths in fast_results.items():
                result_dict[map_type] = paths
                map_result.engines[map_type] = _fast_map.FAST_MAP

            # Shapefile outputs (inundation boundary) are moved by store_maps
            # but not included in its TIF-oriented return dict — glob them,
            # restricted to files produced by this run.
            if "inundation_boundary" in requested_types and not result_dict.get("inundation_boundary"):
                shp_paths = sorted(
                    p for p in plan_output.glob("*.shp")
                    if p.stat().st_mtime >= plan_run_started
                )
                if shp_paths:
                    result_dict["inundation_boundary"] = shp_paths

            for map_type in requested_types:
                tif_paths = result_dict.get(map_type, [])

                # Raster post-processing does not apply to shapefile outputs
                if map_type != "inundation_boundary":
                    # Post-process: depth threshold
                    if map_type == "depth" and min_depth > 0.0:
                        tif_paths = _apply_depth_threshold(tif_paths, min_depth)

                    # Post-process: reproject to WGS84
                    if reproject_wgs84:
                        tif_paths = _reproject_tifs(tif_paths, "EPSG:4326")

                    # Post-process: convert to COG
                    if convert_cog:
                        tif_paths = _convert_to_cog(tif_paths, map_type=map_type)

                if tif_paths:
                    map_result.map_types[map_type] = tif_paths
                    console.print(f"    {map_type}: {len(tif_paths)} raster(s)")

            postprocessing_hdf = plan_output / "PostProcessing.hdf"
            if postprocessing_hdf.exists() and not keep_postprocessing:
                size_mb = postprocessing_hdf.stat().st_size / 1e6
                postprocessing_hdf.unlink()
                console.print(f"    Removed PostProcessing.hdf cache ({size_mb:.0f} MB)")

        except Exception as e:
            error_msg = f"plan {plan_id}: {e}"
            map_result.errors.append(error_msg)
            console.print(f"    [yellow]Warning:[/yellow] {error_msg}")
            if not skip_errors:
                raise

        results.append(map_result)

    total_maps = sum(
        sum(len(paths) for paths in r.map_types.values())
        for r in results
    )
    total_errors = sum(len(r.errors) for r in results)
    console.print(f"\n[green]OK[/green] Generated {total_maps} raster(s) from {len(results)} plan(s)")
    if total_errors:
        console.print(f"  [yellow]{total_errors} error(s)[/yellow]")

    return results

ras2cng.pmtiles
docs.text:
PMTiles generation for the ras2cng pmtiles CLI surface.

Vector tiles: - GeoParquet -> reproject to EPSG:4326 -> newline-delimited GeoJSON -> tippecanoe -> PMTiles, or GeoParquet -> freestiler -> PMTiles when RAS2CNG_VECTOR_TILER resolves to freestiler (see :mod:ras2cng.vector_tiles). A freestiler with Arrow input reads the GeoParquet as an Arrow table and reprojects it in Rust (in Python with pyproj when it refuses the CRS); older builds get a GeoDataFrame.

Raster tiles: - delegated to :mod:ras2cng.maplibre, which colorizes at native resolution, warps to an exact Web Mercator zoom, and builds the tile pyramid.

Note: tippecanoe, gdal, and pmtiles are command-line tools and must be installed separately and available on PATH. freestiler is the optional ras2cng[freestiler] extra.

:mod:ras2cng.maplibre is the maintained implementation of both jobs and streams its inputs; this module is the older single-file CLI surface kept for ras2cng pmtiles.

docs.title: generate_mesh_pmtiles(input_file, output, *, layer_name='mesh_cells', mesh_names=None, properties=None, min_zoom=10, max_zoom=14, source_crs=None, threads=None)
docs.text:
Tile HDF mesh cells through Rust, using pyproj for bulk reprojection.

Requires the separately built ras-commander-fast-hdf extension. The source may be geometry HDF or a computed plan containing geometry. Properties are column arrays keyed by mesh name, indexed by original cell ID. All selected meshes share a source layer, with mesh_name/cell_id properties preserving identity. This explicit HDF route does not use the GeoParquet tiler selector.

Source code in ras2cng/pmtiles.py 
def generate_mesh_pmtiles(
    input_file: Path,
    output: Path,
    *,
    layer_name: str = "mesh_cells",
    mesh_names: Optional[list[str]] = None,
    properties: Optional[dict] = None,
    min_zoom: int = 10,
    max_zoom: int = 14,
    source_crs: Optional[str] = None,
    threads: Optional[int] = None,
) -> Path:
    """Tile HDF mesh cells through Rust, using pyproj for bulk reprojection.

    Requires the separately built ras-commander-fast-hdf extension. The source
    may be geometry HDF or a computed plan containing geometry. Properties are
    column arrays keyed by mesh name, indexed by original cell ID. All selected
    meshes share a source layer, with mesh_name/cell_id properties preserving
    identity. This explicit HDF route does not use the GeoParquet tiler selector.
    """
    from ras_commander.fast_hdf import export_mesh_pmtiles
    from ras2cng.cog import atomic_output

    input_file = Path(input_file)
    output = Path(output)
    if input_file.resolve() == output.resolve():
        raise ValueError("Output must not replace the source HDF")
    with atomic_output(output, suffix=".pmtiles") as staged:
        export_mesh_pmtiles(
            input_file, staged, layer_name=layer_name, mesh_names=mesh_names,
            properties=properties, min_zoom=min_zoom, max_zoom=max_zoom,
            source_crs=source_crs, threads=threads, backend="rust",
        )
    return output

docs.text:
Render a numeric raster to PNG PMTiles via the maplibre pipeline.

This used to run gdal_translate -of MBTiles -co TILE_FORMAT=PNG directly on the source. Against a float32 depth or WSE COG that produces an 8-bit image with no color ramp and no alpha -- nodata renders as opaque black -- and it built no overviews at all, so the MINZOOM creation option had nothing to apply to.

:func:ras2cng.maplibre._render_raster_pmtiles is the correct implementation of this job: it applies the color ramp at native resolution before any downsampling, warps to an exact Web Mercator zoom resolution, and builds the pyramid.

Source code in ras2cng/pmtiles.py 
def generate_raster_pmtiles(
    input_file: Path,
    output: Path,
    min_zoom: Optional[int] = None,
    max_zoom: Optional[int] = None,
    *,
    map_type: str = "depth",
):
    """Render a numeric raster to PNG PMTiles via the maplibre pipeline.

    This used to run ``gdal_translate -of MBTiles -co TILE_FORMAT=PNG`` directly
    on the source.  Against a float32 depth or WSE COG that produces an 8-bit
    image with no color ramp and no alpha -- nodata renders as opaque black --
    and it built no overviews at all, so the ``MINZOOM`` creation option had
    nothing to apply to.

    :func:`ras2cng.maplibre._render_raster_pmtiles` is the correct
    implementation of this job: it applies the color ramp at native resolution
    before any downsampling, warps to an exact Web Mercator zoom resolution, and
    builds the pyramid.
    """

    from ras2cng import maplibre

    input_path = Path(input_file)
    output = Path(output)
    output.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    backend = maplibre._raster_backend_for(input_path)

    info = maplibre._gdalinfo(input_path)
    bands = info.get("bands") or []
    if not bands:
        raise ValueError(f"Raster has no readable bands: {input_path}")
    band = bands[0]
    stats = {
        "minimum": float(band.get("minimum", 0.0)),
        "maximum": float(band.get("maximum", 1.0)),
    }

    def ramp_writer(path: Path) -> None:
        maplibre._result_color_ramp(stats, map_type, path)

    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix="ras2cng-raster-pmtiles-") as scratch:
        maplibre._render_raster_pmtiles(
            input_path,
            output,
            ramp_writer=ramp_writer,
            max_zoom=max_zoom,
            scratch_dir=Path(scratch),
            prefix="cli-raster",
            backend=backend,
        )

def sync_to_postgres(
    input_file: Path,
    postgres_uri: str,
    table_name: str,
    schema: str = "public",
    if_exists: str = "replace",
):
    """Sync a GeoParquet file to a PostGIS table."""

    from ras2cng.geoparquet import flatten_bbox_struct

    # PostGIS has its own GiST index; the GeoParquet ``bbox`` struct of
    # schema-2.7 archives is stored as the same four float columns that older
    # archives carry, so the table shape does not depend on the archive version.
    gdf = flatten_bbox_struct(gpd.read_parquet(input_file))

    engine = create_engine(postgres_uri)

    # Ensure schema exists
    with engine.begin() as conn:
        conn.execute(text(f"CREATE SCHEMA IF NOT EXISTS {schema}"))

    # Write table
    gdf.to_postgis(
        table_name,
        engine,
        schema=schema,
        if_exists=if_exists,
        index=False,
    )

    # Spatial index
    if "geometry" in gdf.columns:
        idx_name = f"{table_name}_geom_idx"
        with engine.begin() as conn:
            conn.execute(
                text(
                    f'CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS "{idx_name}" ON {schema}."{table_name}" USING GIST (geometry)'
                )
            )

def read_from_postgres(
    postgres_uri: str,
    table_name: str,
    schema: str = "public",
    geometry_column: str = "geometry",
) -> gpd.GeoDataFrame:
    """Read a PostGIS table to a GeoDataFrame."""

    engine = create_engine(postgres_uri)
    sql = f"SELECT * FROM {schema}.\"{table_name}\""
    return gpd.read_postgis(sql, engine, geom_col=geometry_column)

Read gridded precipitation raster metadata from a HEC-RAS HDF file.

The HDF must include raster georeferencing attributes: Raster Rows, Raster Cols, Raster Cellsize, Raster Left, and Raster Top. Projection WKT and units are preserved when present.
